### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/hono`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/test-typecheck-debt.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bc764332aecfb63345e2abd5d2a3c1b550e114f`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/test-typecheck-debt.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bc764332aecfb63345e2abd5d2a3c1b550e114f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `37a7f242a78b59541767b9e4befdb96811ceda0f` — the merge of head `533f8da14dabc67b793283120aaa297e10b753bf` into base `6bc764332aecfb63345e2abd5d2a3c1b550e114f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 37a7f242a78b59541767b9e4befdb96811ceda0f && git checkout 37a7f242a78b59541767b9e4befdb96811ceda0f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6bc764332aecfb63345e2abd5d2a3c1b550e114f 533f8da14dabc67b793283120aaa297e10b753bf && git checkout -B drift-repro 6bc764332aecfb63345e2abd5d2a3c1b550e114f && git merge --no-ff 533f8da14dabc67b793283120aaa297e10b753bf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bc764332aecfb63345e2abd5d2a3c1b550e114f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6bc764332aecfb63345e2abd5d2a3c1b550e114f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgXcN9HaZYSEUdJWEjw

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `75d7d9e115f02073fd761a170cad7eece9367359`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs, packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-forward.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution-destructive.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/api-action-door-forward.dogfood.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/index.ts (what `@objectstack/runtime` publishes), packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts (the `response.headers` consumer), packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts (the second in-repo consumer), packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts (`IHttpResponse.header`, `getRawApp`), packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts (the `server.trustProxy` rule), packages/types/src/in-process-session-read.ts (cookie-session admission), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`run_action` result rendering), ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx and ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/resolvePageVarTokens.ts (the console's api body rules), docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md D4, docs/adr/0126-packaged-metadata-customization-model.md §4/§8, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts (`requiredPermissions` docblock), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.actions-type-dispatch.test.ts (the untouched pin the diff flips), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`breakingDeclaration`), .changeset/27506-api-action-door-forward.md and content/docs/ui/actions.mdx (prose: ② and the contradiction check only). Face: `narrowing` (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Cited code read on `origin/main` `144702ca5dd1` in a detached checkout; head lines from `git show 75d7d9e1:path`.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-29T16:28Z (first read 2026-10-29T16:18Z): `Test Core (3/8)` **failure** (annotation: `command (packages/runtime) pnpm run test exited (1)`); `Test Core (4/8)` and `(5/8)` still `in_progress`; every other non-skipped check `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, the six Test Core shards that completed). The job log sits on a blob host this session's proxy refuses, so the failing case below is read off the tree, not the log.

### ① Derived judgments

Widenings the diff implies — each named right:
- `POST /actions/:object/:action` and MCP `run_action` accept a `type: 'api'` action whose `target` starts with `/` (not `//`, not `/\`) and forward it in-process after the door's own gates (`isHeadlessInvokableAction` head 1013-1016, `headlessActionTypeError` head 1491; `domains/actions.ts` head 830-863; `invokeBusinessAction` head 3253-3283). **Right** — the ruling's letter C, step 2.
- MCP `list_actions` lists such actions without a handler-registry hit (`domains/mcp.ts` head 837). **Right.**
- `HttpDispatcherResult.response.headers` accepts `string[]` (`http-dispatcher.ts` head 160) and the hono plugin's route `res.header` appends an array one line per element (`adapter.ts` head 816-828). **Right as a mechanism** — `IHttpResponse.header(name, value: string | string[])` was already the contract (`packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts:100`), and the plugin's middleware-seam response at `adapter.ts:1530` already appended arrays; the route seam was the one that did not.

Narrowings the diff implies — each named right, with one wrong carrier:
- `POST /actions/_activation/:object/:action` refuses, 409, to flip a `type: 'api'` action whose `target` is not a same-origin path, in both directions, after the authority gates (`domains/actions.ts` head 239-244, step 3b after step 1's two authority refusals — the 409 discloses nothing to an ungranted caller). Before the diff that request answered 200 and wrote a ledger row. **Right, and it is THE narrowing of a REST answer this PR makes**: a row already written for an off-origin api action can no longer be flipped back on, which is the one thing a deployer could notice. The `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` arm is therefore **right**. Its rationale sentence on the PR body and the changeset ("an api action that reaches the doors now passes their gates … where the console's direct fetch passed none") names a widening of the doors (they answered 400 to the type before) and a comparison with a path this PR does not change (the console still fetches `target` directly until #27611); it does not name the 409. The arm stands; the sentence is corrected under ② (should-fix).
- Both doors refuse an off-origin api action 400 with a new message naming the origin (head 1497-1509). **Right** — a 400 before, a 400 now; the message is the only change.
- MCP `run_action` on a same-origin api action is no longer refused for its type; the system-object guard (`isSystemObjectName`, head 2686) still refuses every `sys_*` object ahead of it, so none of the 13 identity actions is reachable over MCP. **Right as code**; the ruling's sentence "`list_actions` and `run_action` expose them to agents with no further change" is not true for the actions the card is about — see ③.

Published surface:
- `@objectstack/runtime` publishes only `src/index.ts` (package.json `exports["."]`), which re-exports nothing from `action-execution.ts` — the eleven new exports there (`isSameOriginApiTarget`, `isSameOriginApiAction`, `offOriginApiActivationRefusal`, `API_FORWARD_MARK_HEADER`, `buildApiActionRequest`, `resolveInProcessRequest`, `apiActionForwardUnavailableError`, `apiActionForwardLoopError`, `forwardApiAction`, `apiActionResultOf`, `apiActionForwardRefusal` and the three types) are package-internal. **No new published symbol.** `isSameOriginApiAction` (head 1075) has no caller in the tree — should-fix (dead export).
- `HttpDispatcherResult` IS published (`index.ts:212`, `export type { HttpProtocolContext, HttpDispatcherResult }`), so widening `response.headers` from `Record<string, string>` to `Record<string, string | string[]>` **changes a published type**: for a producer it widens; for a consumer that reads the field (a host adapter) it is a breaking type change — a reader typed to `string` no longer compiles without a cast. The in-repo reader `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts:471-474` hands the value to `IHttpResponse.header`, which takes the array — fine. The second in-repo reader, the published `@objectstack/hono` adapter (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:764` and `:861`), casts `v as string` and hands the array to Hono's `c.header`, which stringifies it comma-joined — the exact `Set-Cookie` defect this diff fixes in the plugin. On that host the forward itself answers 503 (no `http.server` service is registered there, so `resolveInProcessRequest` is null), so this producer cannot reach it today; but the published type now says arrays may arrive and that published consumer mishandles them. **Should-fix**: update that consumer in the same change, and name the type change in the BREAKING banner (②).
- `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` publishes `adapter.ts` wholesale (`src/index.ts` `export * from './adapter'`); the route `res.header` parameter type widening is the contract's own signature — no new symbol, no breaking read.

Declaration line: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — **right**; `Metadata-protocol: none` — **right** (no authorable key, value or meaning changes in `packages/spec`; the `semantic` change rides #27610). The BREAKING carriers: AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist step 3 says the `(narrowing)` arm "is BREAKING" and that a non-protocol breaking change "ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"; precedent #26801 (the same `no (narrowing)` of a REST answer, `patch`, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) carried `fix(plugin-security)!:` in its title and a `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing …` paragraph with Before / Now / Unchanged / Who sees it / The remedy in its changeset. This changeset carries the disposition marker but no `**BREAKING**` banner (zero occurrences), and the PR title carries no `!`. `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` `breakingDeclaration` reads the arm alone as a breaking signal, so no gate reds — which is exactly why the rule text has to be applied by review. **Ruling: this narrowing owes both.** The banner is a must-fix on the declaration carriers (the rule says it is kept; it is the sentence an upgrading agent greps in `CHANGELOG.md`); the `!` travels with it (the squash subject is the commit this gate's `bang` signal reads).

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/runtime': patch`, `'@objectstack/plugin-hono-server': patch` — **right for the kind**: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and the rule keeps `patch` for a non-protocol breaking change. No other published package moves: `@objectstack/spec` is untouched, `@objectstack/mcp` is untouched, `scripts/` publishes nothing, the dogfood package is private.

What the changeset owes before it is right (all on the same file, one edit):
1. **Must-fix** — a `**BREAKING**` paragraph (the #26801 shape): Before (the activation write door recorded a flip for any declared action), Now (409 for a `type: 'api'` action whose `target` is not a same-origin path, both directions, no ledger row), Who sees it (a deployment that already switched such an action, or an app declaring one), The remedy (point the `target` at a same-origin path, or remove the action — the refusal's own sentence). Add the published-type change: `HttpDispatcherResult.response.headers` may now hold `string[]`; a host adapter that reads it hands each element to `IHttpResponse.header` (which takes the array) — the one-line fix.
2. **Should-fix** — the `Clause-②:` rationale sentence names the 409 above (the narrowing) rather than the doors' new acceptance (a widening) — the arm is right, the reason is not.
3. **Should-fix** — the ADR-0087 marker's `why` says "no … export … changes meaning; an app upgrades with no edit". A host adapter built against the published `HttpDispatcherResult` needs the edit above; `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` stays (the prescription is one line and lives in the banner, as #26801 did), but the `why` must not deny the type change.

Prose check: `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` now says a same-origin `type: 'api'` action is dispatched through the doors. On the tree this record reviews, `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md:74` (D4, 2026-07 scope note) and `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts:1596-1606` (the `requiredPermissions` docblock and `.describe()`, which `check:docs` renders) say the opposite — "fetched by the browser directly and never passes through that route". The doc sentence is contradicted by the tree until #27610 lands; that is the landing order the ruling set, not a defect of this diff, and it is why this record does not authorise landing ahead of #27610 (③).

### ③ Boundary flags

Every flag in the dev's os-dev-report (6502065277) and the ruling's execution text, answered or escalated:
- **File surface grew beyond the claim's three files** (`http-dispatcher.ts`, `plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`): answered — both are the cookie lane's mechanism and the re-claim's "stop on breach and explain in the report" was honoured in the report. Ruled in ①: the header type is a published-type change and must be carried by the banner; the second in-repo reader (`@objectstack/hono`) was missed — should-fix.
- **MCP `run_action` still refuses every `sys_*` object** (class b, "carrier: person — noted, not filed"): escalated to the seat. The ruling's step 2 says the predicate change "exposes them to agents with no further change"; the system-object guard (`action-execution.ts` head 2686 and `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:1294`) means an agent reaches `ban_user`, `impersonate_user`, `set_user_password` only through the REST `/actions` door. "Person" is not a carrier: Prime Directive #10 wants a card (the guard's own prior decision versus the maintainer's design goal) or an explicit acceptance on #27506 by the seat. Not a defect of this diff; it is a gap between the ruling's text and the tree that must be recorded somewhere a reader finds it.
- **Non-JSON targets** (print → `/api/v1/print/records`, relayed as `{ raw: text }`): escalated. The door forces `accept: application/json` (head 1394) and answers 200 with a binary body decoded as text in `{ raw }` (head 1417) — a machine-readable surface that lies (Route & surface ownership rule 4). #27611's body routes every same-origin api click through the door and does not name this case, so the carrier the report names does not carry it. Should-fix on the door (refuse a non-JSON answer loudly with the status and content type, or relay it as bytes) or an amendment to #27611's body by the seat — one of the two, in writing.
- **`{{page.*}}` / `${ctx.selection.*}` tokens left to #27611**: answered — #27611's body already says page-variable tokens stay client-side and travel as `params`; the door's 400 by name is the loud half. One should-fix rides on it (④: the page-token detector is wider than the console's grammar).
- **Landing gated on #27610** (Tier H): answered — the PR body, the dev report and the re-claim all state it; the only mechanical hold is the draft flag. **This record, whatever its verdict, does not lift that order**: ADR-0066 D4 and the spec docblock on `main` still record the decision this diff reverses, and Prime Directive #13 puts the ADR edit first.
- **Branch name** `claude/project-thread-lzb7u9` (not `claude/issue-27506-*`): answered — the re-claim records it as the harness-pinned branch, a measured platform exception; `Implemented-by:` below carries it.
- `open_questions: []` — nothing further to answer.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the ruling's scenario (one system for people and agents: a switched-off packaged api action refused at every door, an on api action invocable headlessly through the same doors) and against the code each hunk cites.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`** — holds, with one must-fix elsewhere pinned here. The api arm (head 830-863) sits after the anonymous floor (427-460), the disabled-package refusal (548-556), the D4 gate (637-640), the ADR-0126 consult (655-664), the type check, the body/param contract (719-726), the subject load (734-737) and `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` (head 823), and before the trusted-mode `actionContext` — so every gate the door already ran still runs first, and an api action never receives the system-elevated facade. The target's own gates run after the forward because the forward is an ordinary in-process request through `app.request` (the dogfood pins a member's 403 and an anonymous 401 at the door). The two relayed answers spread `deps.success` / `deps.error` and add `headers` (head 846-855), and the route-envelope ledger declares them (`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` `handBuilt: 3`, with the note the ledger requires; the lint gate is green). Step 3b of the activation write (head 239-244) is after both authority refusals — right. **The untouched pin `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.actions-type-dispatch.test.ts:350-366`** ("points a `type: api` action at the endpoint it actually dispatches on") asserts `400` for `{ type: 'api', target: '/api/v1/auth/organization/create-team' }` through a fixture that resolves no `http.server` (lines 73-82); under this diff that call reaches the api arm and answers `503` (`apiActionForwardUnavailableError`), which is the `packages/runtime` red in `Test Core (3/8)`. **Must-fix**: rewrite the pin to the contract this diff sets (the forward through an injector, and the 503 on a kernel with none) — never delete it (a test is deleted only when its PR names a duplicate pin at a layer at least as close). The report's "128/128" covered four files, not the package suite the shard runs.

**`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`** — the design holds; three findings.
- Same-origin test (`isSameOriginApiTarget`, head 1065-1072): a path starting with `/` whose second character is neither `/` nor `\`. Tried: `https://same-host:other-port/…` → refused as off-origin (conservative: such an action becomes browser-only and unswitchable; acceptable, the console's `sameOriginOnly` lane treats an absolute URL the same way); `//host` and `/\host` → refused; an encoded `/%2F%2F…` → stays in-process (`app.request` routes on the path; no origin escape); a `${param.*}` or `{field}` value is percent-encoded before it lands in the path (head 1140-1141, 1207-1210) and the interpolated path is re-tested (head 1226), so a param cannot turn a same-origin template into `//…`; a target that is an action door → the forward carries `x-objectstack-action-forward` and both doors refuse a request bearing it (head 3253-3258; `domains/actions.ts` head 831-834), the MCP door included because its `context.request.headers` is the same lower-cased `c.req.header()` map (`adapter.ts:728`); a target on another door (`/data/...`, `/automation/.../trigger`) runs that door's own gates with the caller's own credentials — no weaker gate is reachable than by calling it directly. Holds.
- Credentials forwarded (`API_FORWARD_HEADER_ALLOWLIST`, head 1105-1114): the caller's `authorization`, `cookie`, `x-admin-session-token`, `x-api-key`, tenant/environment ids, `origin`/`referer`/`user-agent`/`accept-language`, and the proxy provenance headers; nothing else crosses, `host` and `content-length` are the injector's, `accept` is forced. No header the caller does not already control is added except the loop mark. Holds — the forward carries exactly the admitted principal. **Should-fix (security hardening, mechanism only)**: head 1401-1406 build the injected URL's origin from the caller-controlled `x-forwarded-host` / `x-forwarded-proto` unconditionally; the platform's one forwarded-header trust rule is `server.trustProxy` (`packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts:130-141`, `resolveClientAddress`), and no other site in `packages/` reads `x-forwarded-host`. Read `host` only, or honour `server.trustProxy`. Detail in the seat's evidence file.
- Relay back (head 1424-1433): `set-auth-token`, `set-admin-session-token`, and every `Set-Cookie` line as an array. On the REST door this is the ruling's own order and the hono plugin now emits one line per element — right. **Must-fix (security, mechanism only)**: the MCP arm returns the same `headers` object inside the tool result (head 3280), and `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:1298-1306` renders it as JSON text; the MCP door admits cookie sessions (`packages/types/src/in-process-session-read.ts:94-106` reads the `cookie` header for every in-process session read), so a cookie-lane caller receives HttpOnly session-cookie values inside a JSON body, which is what HttpOnly exists to prevent. The MCP transport has no cookie consumer; relay only the bearer-lane pair there. Detail in the seat's evidence file.
- Body assembly (`buildApiActionRequest`, head 1184-1300) against the console's `apiHandler` (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:411-497`): same order — `{field}` from the row, `bodyShape.wrap`, the `outputs.*` fold, `recordIdParam` seeded or refused by name (#8018), `organizationId` for an `/api/v1/auth/` target, `bodyExtra` last, `method`, no body on GET/DELETE (the console sends no query string for GET either, so parity holds). Two divergences: the console injects `organizationId` when the value is falsy, the door only when `undefined` (negligible); **should-fix** — `carriesPageToken` (head 1154-1159) refuses any string containing `{{`, while the console's grammar is `{{page.path}}` (`resolvePageVarTokens.ts:27,47`), so a legitimate param value or `bodyExtra` string carrying `{{` is refused 400 for a token it does not carry — match the grammar.
- Error envelopes: a non-2xx answer rides the target's own status and code (head 1467-1480, `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus` as the fallback); a 3xx is folded into that refusal shape with no `Location` (no packaged action targets a redirecting route — noted, not a finding); a non-JSON answer is a 200 with `{ raw }` under a forced JSON `accept` — should-fix per ③; an empty body is `null`. The result unwraps `data` only when the body carries both `success` and `data` (head 1448-1452), one notch stricter than the console's `'data' in json` — right (a bare better-auth body with a `data` key is not an envelope).
- MCP type gate: `isHeadlessInvokableAction` admits a same-origin api target with or without an automation service — right; `offOriginApiActivationRefusal` (head 1089-1101) names "off-origin" for a target that is absent or not a string as well — the sentence is slightly wrong for a target-less declaration (nit).
- `isSameOriginApiAction` (head 1075) — exported, never called: should-fix.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`** — holds. The listing skips the handler-registry check for `type: 'api'` exactly as for `flow` and the declarative update (head 837), after the `sys_*` fail-closed line and `isHeadlessInvokableAction`, before the `ai.exposed` gate; `run_action` is unchanged here and takes `invokeBusinessAction`'s sequence (exposure → D4 → consult → params → confirmation → subject load → `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` → api arm). The dogfood pins the gate order on the live transport.

**`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`** — holds as a mechanism; it is a published-type change (①, ②) and one published consumer mishandles it (①).

**`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`** — holds.
